description: The arguments that policies see (docs/contracts/module-contract-v0.1.md, section 6.11, EP-19). transforms: the four transforms, each case with transform, lowercase, path, url_host or email_domain; value, the string; and result, what the transform gives, or null when it cannot read the value. The cases with the IDs of the URL and address check (inputs/url-and-address-check.json) take its values, L01 to X38 as url_host reads them and E01 to F15 as email_domain does, and I01 to I14 its hosts of IDNA, in its order, as email_domain reads alice@ and the host; their results come from section 6.11. records: a tool's record of context.args, as EP-19 fills it. Each case gives args, the tool's declared arguments as the catalog file lists them (section 7.7): name, the key in the record; path, the property names that lead to the argument; transform, when one applies; and type, String, Long, Bool, Set<String> or Set<Long>; the call's arguments, as a JSON value in arguments or, where a parsed value cannot hold them, as their text in arguments_text, and neither when the call has none, which is an empty object; and record, the declared arguments that the call has, each under its name, with its transform applied, a set written as its distinct elements in ascending order, or null when EP-19 denies the call with error.invalid_request: arguments that are not a JSON object, or that repeat a member name, whatever the tool declares; a path through a value that is not an object, or through an object that repeats a member name; or a declared argument's value that does not fit its declared type, null and a string with a lone surrogate included, or that its transform cannot read. A missing argument is left out of the record, so that usage rules apply if_absent.
